Zokka (F29)

Survey region (English ranking table): Bulwar.

1444 starting country: Zokka (F29)

In brief: Zokka turns “Devourer of Suns” from a boast into the campaign's objective. First, survive a decisive opening war with Jaddari; then expand through raiding, demonic rites, devouring rulers, and slave factions until you tear open Hell and devour the Moon and Sun. The story is spectacular, and it depends almost entirely on continuous war.

Story: Extremely high | Mission tree: Enormous (58 direct missions in the current local scripts) | Mission-tree update: Verified locally against v1.37.5.0 | Distinctiveness: Extremely high | Tedium: Extremely high | Early pressure: Extremely high | Expansion: Extremely high

Identity and History

Zokka (F29) is a Sandfang Gnoll pack available at the 1444 start. The country follows Xhazobkult and is ruled by Zokka, lord of the pack bearing his name. He has ruled since 1435, is a bold and aggressive military mage, and his dynastic title openly proclaims him the “Devourer-of-Suns.” [Local history script]

Zokka has crossed the Salahad desert and is pressing into Bulwar. His rule rests on plunder, enslavement, demonic bargains, and personal intimidation. In the official setting timeline, Jaddar kills Zokka in a decisive battle; the player campaign begins by overturning that fate. [Local flavor text] [Official development diary]

The offline Wiki says Zokka's power stretched from Far Salahad to the Upper Suran and that he collected tribute from several cities. After suppressing a human rebellion in 1443, he agreed with Tluukt to divide the Suran. The official setting timeline places his death in the 1445 Battle of Sun's Providence: his followers then disband, flee to Tluukt, or are absorbed into the Jadd. This is the setting's default outcome, not an inevitable result of a player campaign. [Wiki]

National Story and Campaign Arc

The opening Zokka–Jaddar war is not an ordinary border conflict. The rulers' duel decides which imperial route survives: if Zokka loses, he dies and the player switches to Tluukt; if Jaddar loses, Zokka gains much of his land and Bulwar's history shifts from the prologue to a sunlit empire into a demonic conquest. [Local event]

Afterward, the missions move from subjugating other Gnolls and burning centers of the Sun faith to expansion across North Sarhal, the Forbidden Plains, Haless, Yanshen, the Serpentspine, and still more distant lands. Ordinary countries accumulate territory; Zokka frames each conquest as a sacrifice, a meal, or supplies for the final rite. [Local missions] [Local flavor text]

Core Mechanics

Xhazobkult and the raiding cycle. Razing newly conquered land, lighting pyres, raiding coasts, and establishing local cults can replenish money, monarch points, and Demonic Power. Zokka does not stabilize first and fight later: the next war must finance the resources consumed by the last one. [Local religion mechanics] [Local localization]

Devouring rulers. Once the special ability is obtained, a dedicated peace treaty becomes available in wars of demonic invasion. After occupying an enemy capital, Zokka can devour its ruler, gaining monarch points and Demonic Power according to that ruler's abilities, while also forcing the defeated country to release nations and subjects. The war goal shifts from “how much land is worth taking?” to “which ruler is most valuable to eat?” [Local peace treaty] [Local localization]

Kaxhkeddax and Kelmaxherho. The two dedicated estates represent destruction, sacrifice, and tradition on one side, and integration, preservation, and pragmatism on the other. The current English localization calls the Kelmaxherho a caste made predominantly of non-Gnollish scholar-slaves. Missions and events repeatedly grant favor to each estate; favoring one weakens the other, while maintaining a difficult balance may yield greater rewards. [Local missions] [Local localization]

Great Xhaz and the demonic empire. Missions lead Zokka to absorb demonic power, transform the government, open higher temples and a Hellgate, and devour supernatural beings such as Xhazob, Khet, and the Great Spirits. This is not simply a powerful mage state: the entire country becomes part of a sacrificial system for the ruler's apotheosis. [Local missions] [Local flavor text]

Devour the Moon and Sun. Late events rename the country “Sunkiller Xhaz” and shift the goal from continental conquest to a cosmic scale. After the Moon is devoured, Halann enters a global crisis; the final mission demands more conquest and sacrifice, and a genuine challenge to the Sun. [Local missions] [Local events]

Staged Play

Opening showdown: Your first priority is ensuring Zokka and his main force win the decisive clash with Jaddar. Losing does not mean an ordinary peace: Zokka's route ends and the country changes to Tluukt. Concentrate your forces early instead of scattering them over secondary objectives.

Conquest of Bulwar: After victory, use razing and peace reparations to sustain money, monarch points, and Demonic Power; use monstrous mercenaries to absorb manpower losses when needed. The rhythm is continuous war, not waiting for the domestic economy to recover on its own.

Factions and intercontinental expansion: Once the Kaxhkeddax and Kelmaxherho appear, choose between total destruction, pragmatic integration, or a balance between them. Meanwhile, the missions pull the front across several continents; tributaries and subjects can reduce the burden of direct rule.

Cosmic endgame: The Hellgate, devouring gods, and Moon events turn the late game into a world-scale catastrophe. Military superiority is usually already established; the real pressure shifts to moving armies between continents, coring, rebellions, colonial range, and long mission requirements.

Mission Future and Endgame

No formable country or successor Tag has been confirmed for Zokka. The country remains F29 and is only renamed “Sunkiller Xhaz” by a late event. Its development is not a Tag-switch upgrade: it follows Zokka himself from Gnoll warlord to a being capable of devouring gods, the Moon, and the Sun. [Local event]

The official development diary announced 57 missions; the current local files yield a deterministic count of 58 direct missions. This article uses the local v1.37.5.0 count for current implementation and retains 57 as the count at the time of the diary. [Official development diary] [Local missions]

Personality and Recommendation

v2.1 personality coordinates: Expansion 100/100 | Autocracy 95/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 100/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; theme intensity 100/100) | Pluralism 10/100.

v2.1 values: Evil (0/100), with a stable trajectory. Enslavement, sacrifice, devouring enemy rulers, and destructive demonic goals run through the main campaign and directly harm nearly every values dimension.

Recommended for players who enjoy an extreme villain's arc, continuous warfare, resource snowballing, strongly defined factions, and an absurd cosmic finale. Not recommended if you prefer peaceful development, stable diplomacy, low-micro campaigns, or do not want enslavement, sacrifice, and world-destruction themes.

Community Experience

Community view: A 28 July 2025 help thread reflects how new players can run short of manpower, money, monarch points, and Demonic Power at the same time. Highly relevant replies commonly recommend frequent razing, monstrous mercenaries, coastal raiding, and establishing cult sites early. It shows that the intended resource cycle is not intuitive.

Community view: A 30 August 2026 campaign report demonstrates Zokka's extreme expansion potential, but the author used the console after 1497 to open Insyaa, which was blocked by the Stormwall, and kept Serpentspine subjects. It is not evidence of a strict, unmodified, single-Tag world conquest by 1501.

Evidence Boundaries

This article concerns base Mod and translation v1.37.5.0, checked 16 September 2026. Tag, current Chinese display name, opening ruler, the Zokka–Jaddar war, 58 direct missions, the devouring peace treaty, the two estates, and the late renaming all come from current local files. The offline Wiki was reread for Zokka (page_id=917, revision_id=32372), Tluukt (916/21322), and Sandfang Gnoll (2883/32494), supplementing the pack's reach, alliance, Sandfang background, and default setting outcome. Reddit is used only for official design context and two player experiences. Full sources and conflicts are in the evidence record.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Zokka (F29) — Zokka Ideas

Set ID: F29_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = F29 #Zokka
    }

Zokka Traditions

  • Infantry shock: +15% (infantry_shock; raw value 0.15).

  • Subject liberty desire: +1000% (reduced_liberty_desire; raw value 10).

1. The First Sun Slayers

For Zokka, new to leadership of a Far Salahad gnoll pack, it was just another day hunting in the harsh desert heat. An insufficiently guarded caravan, demonically-enhanced strength, a brutal ambush; the story writes itself. His pack ate well that night, dining on their slaughtered foes. A strong success for the new pack-leader, but nothing more notable than that.

For the elves of Sareyand, who awaited a caravan that never arrived, and found little but sun-scorched bones when they looked for it — it was horror. A whisper of an age long past, an age thought banished forevermore by Surael's incarnation Jaher. For those Sun Elves Zokka had made a meal of were the first elves to be devoured by gnolls in centuries. A force was mustered to confront the gnoll. It came back battered, scorched by demonflame. The next simply vanished into the sands. Even the Desert Legion could not hunt him down. And all the while, in the Salahad, the legend of Zokka, Devourer-of-Suns, grew and grew.

  • Province warscore cost: -15% (province_warscore_cost; raw value -0.15).

2. An Economy of Plundering

Out of the arid Salahad, various peoples make coin in various ways. The Desert Legion pursues the staid job of caravan-guards, the Mašnsih tend their flocks, merchants of east and west grow rich selling to the other side. But the gnolls of Zokka know the best way. Just loot everyone else's! Ever since that first caravan, Zokka's horde has plundered everything that can be taken, and destroyed what cannot be, after laying their foes to waste.

  • Looting speed: +50% (loot_amount; raw value 0.5).

3. Shared Goal of Domination

Bulwari children fear Zokka's gnashing teeth. Sareyandi soldiers fear his demonic strength. But the cleverest scholars and most studied generals of the Desert Legion? They fear what truly makes him dangerous, his cunning nature. That trait was on full display when he arranged a meeting with the Matriarch Astárta Siadunó in 1424 AA. They both had dreams of a new 'Age of Monsters'; he sought to resurrect gnollish Bulwar, she hoped to return the harpy matriarchy of Siadanlén to predominance in the Far Salahad. And they both knew those dreams would require the slaughter of Sun Elves, and any else who would stand before them. With the mixing of a drop of harpy and gnollish blood into a bottle of wine, then quaffed by the two rulers, the pact was sealed — and Surael himself must have shivered.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

4. Recruits from the South

Zokka's pack began small, but grew as more and more gnolls heard of his legend and sought to join him. Even after he had consolidated much of the Far Salahad, Zokka knew the value of a constant stream of fresh blood.

When the packs of Kogzalla and Koggraffa to the south swore their loyalty to him, Zokka didn't seek to claim their lands directly, knowing this would put him in conflict with the larger packs of Sarhal. Instead he demanded they send a regular tithe of soldiers and supplies to ensure that his pack were able to replenish any losses to battle or famine swiftly.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

5. Encouraged Harassment

Zokka prizes loyalty — to him — above much else, and as such, his court is dominated by those gnolls who have been with them ever since those early days. Their position is entrenched, unassailable, and they know it. They make sure every new member to the court, behind in clout compared to their fellow comrades, know this too, by harassing and bullying them endlessly.

This makes it incredibly rare for a new gnoll to rise up in status, rarely happening except in the case of a particularly demon-touched individual. As an unintended consequence, it also prevents potential spies who would rather go home with no information than stand another day of torment.

  • global_spy_defence：+25% (global_spy_defence; raw value 0.25).

6. In Communion with Demons

It is said that Zokka came to command his pack by summoning a demon that swallowed the commanding gnoll whole. It is said that in the Salahad's darkest nights, you can still hear her screams drifting on the wind, as that demon tortures her forevermore. Whatever that rumor's truth, it is certain that few if any gnollish tribes are as zealous as Zokka's in consorting with demons to gain unnatural power. From minor rituals at nightfall and dawn, to pre-battle rites, to post-battle sacrifices, the Xhazobkult infuses every piece of life in Zokka's pack.

  • Yearly demonic power: +0.5% (yearly_patriarch_authority; raw value 0.005).

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1).

7. Superior Cultural Values

The strong rule. The weak serve. Power is all that matters.

This philosophy once dominated Bulwar, but the gnolls of Zokka now see the land covered in weak kingdoms that would rather pray to living failures than embrace that truth. No matter. Every gnoll in the pack knows it, is united by it, and will show the weak just what that belief entails. If that takes drowning the land in blood and hellfire, so be it.

  • Culture conversion cost: -10% (culture_conversion_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -7.5% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.075).
